text: {"observations":"The clip is strongly tonal (noisiness 0) throughout. From about 3.0 s to 9.5 s there is one continuous, sustained voiced sound: fundamental steady near 420 Hz at 4.0-5.0 s with harmonics at 830 and 1250 Hz (the 1250 Hz one strongest), then gliding smoothly down through about 330, 245 and 200 Hz to roughly 130 Hz by 9.5 s. Before it, at 0.25-1.9 s, there is a shorter tonal sound with energy around 0.85-2.1 kHz, consistent with a whine. A single 6-second-plus tonal call with a held pitch and slow downward glide matches a dog howl. It is too long and slow for a cat meow (around 1 s), too sustained and low for bird chirps (no energy above 4 kHz), and starts higher and lasts longer than a typical cow moo (about 100-200 Hz, 1-3 s). This is an inference from pitch and duration, and a cow or a cat yowl cannot be fully excluded.","answer":"B"}
